routes.label: Banff
routes.basis: Parks Canada's itinerary page says 130 km from Calgary.

routes.label: Lake Louise
routes.basis: No single official figure. Parks Canada's Yoho page puts Field 213 km from Calgary and 30 km from Lake Louise, which implies about 183 km. Adding 60 km to Banff gives 190 km. Type your own.

routes.label: Canmore
routes.basis: I found no official distance. Type your own.

routes.label: Kananaskis
routes.basis: Sources give different end points, so there is no one official figure. Type your own. Adds the Kananaskis Conservation Pass: day passes are per vehicle, and rental vehicles are not exempt.

routes.label: Field and Yoho
routes.basis: Parks Canada's Yoho directions page says Field is 213 km from Calgary.

routes.label: Jasper by the Icefields Parkway
routes.basis: Parks Canada gives Lake Louise to Jasper as 232 km on the Icefields Parkway. Add your Calgary to Lake Louise leg (about 183 to 190 km, see Lake Louise) and type the total. In winter there are no services between Jasper and Lake Louise, so fill up first.

routes.label: Radium by Highway 93 South
routes.basis: Added up from Parks Canada pages: 130 km to Banff, 41 km on to the Kootenay gate, 94 km through the park, 2 km to Radium.

winterRules.text: Icefields Parkway and Highway 93 South in Banff National Park: winter tires or chains from November 1 to March 31, or any time the road is snow or ice covered. Highway 93 South in Kootenay and Highway 1 in Yoho: October 1 to April 30. Look for the snowflake or M+S mark.
